description: Sync emails from the Gmail labels you choose, one document per email. Earlier emails of a thread come along even when they sit outside the label.
opening: Sync emails from the Gmail labels you select in one Gmail account. Each email is one document. A reply links to the email it answers, and earlier emails of its thread are fetched too, even from outside the selected label. Supported attachments are read, and their text is searchable with the email.

Gmail connects with an App Password, not OAuth. Gmail permissions are not imported, so every synced email is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule on its label. Emails deleted or moved out of a label stay in HydraDB, and label, read and starred changes are not picked up.

notes: A mailbox is personal in Gmail, but HydraDB does not limit its emails to the mailbox owner. Set an access rule on each label that must stay private.
Earlier thread emails fetched from All Mail follow the access rule of the label that brought them in, even when they sit outside that label.

connect.auth: Gmail connects over IMAP with your Gmail address and a Google App Password. It does not use your Google password or OAuth.

credentials.name: access_token
credentials.text: Your Gmail address and the App Password joined by a colon, as one string: `address:app_password`. It is a single field, not two.

steps.title: Turn on 2-Step Verification
steps.text: Turn on 2-Step Verification for the Google account.

steps.title: Create an App Password
steps.text: Generate an App Password for the Google account.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Paste the Gmail address, a colon and the App Password as `access_token`.

steps.title: Select labels
steps.text: HydraDB lists every selectable mailbox of the account, such as `INBOX` and your own labels. Select the labels to sync.

connect.account: One connector reads one Gmail account.

sync.first_sync: Each label reaches back the window set by `lookback_days`. Earlier emails of a new email's thread are also fetched, up to 10 levels back. When they are outside the label or the lookback window, they are looked up in All Mail.
sync.changes: Each sync fetches the emails that arrived in the label since the last sync. Mail moved into a selected label is fetched too when it gets a new IMAP UID, even with an old delivery date.
sync.edits: An email that is already synced is not read again. Label, read and starred changes are not picked up.
sync.deletes: Deleted emails are not removed. An email deleted or moved out of the label stays searchable in HydraDB.
notes: If Gmail resets a mailbox's message numbering, the label is read again from its lookback window.

documents.name: Emails
documents.one_document: One email. An email without a Message-ID is identified by its IMAP UID instead.
documents.title: The email subject.
documents.text: The subject on the first line. Then each non-empty field of the email as a labelled line, sorted by field name: the body, sender, To and CC addresses, Reply-To, delivery time, the account address, the Message-ID, the Message-ID it replies to, the conversation id and the IMAP UID. The body is plain text: HTML is converted and encoded text is decoded. An email with no body uses its subject. The subject is searchable too.
documents.date: When the email was delivered, or its Date header when the delivery time is missing.
documents.files: Named files inside a multipart email are fetched again and read. Their text becomes searchable when the file type is supported and the fetch succeeds. A file sent as the whole email, not inside a multipart email, is not read as an attachment.

attributes.name: from
attributes.text: The sender's address, written as a line of the text. The graph records the email as sent by that address.

attributes.name: to
attributes.text: The To addresses, written as a line of the text. The graph records each address as a recipient.

attributes.name: cc
attributes.text: The CC addresses, written as a line of the text. The graph records each address as copied.

attributes.name: reply_to
attributes.text: The Reply-To addresses, written as a line of the text. They are not added to the graph as people.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: The delivery time, written as a line of the text.

attributes.name: message_id
attributes.text: The email's Message-ID, written as a line of the text. It identifies the email across syncs.

attributes.name: in_reply_to
attributes.text: The Message-ID of the email this one replies to, from the In-Reply-To header or the last References entry. Links the reply to that email.

attributes.name: forwarded_from_id
attributes.text: The Message-ID of the forwarded email inside this one, when it holds exactly one. Links the email to it.

attributes.name: gmail_msg_id
attributes.text: The email's IMAP UID in the mailbox it was read from, which is All Mail for earlier thread emails. It is not a Gmail API message id.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.thread_id
attributes.text: The conversation id: the first Message-ID in the References header, else In-Reply-To, else the email's own Message-ID. Limits a query to one conversation, and groups the conversation's emails in the graph. Also written as a line of the text.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.account_email
attributes.text: The Gmail account address. Limits a query to emails from one account. Also written as a line of the text.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's emails. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Notification links
attributes.text: Links a GitHub or Linear notification email to the GitHub issue or pull request, or the Linear issue, it is about. Only emails from `notifications@github.com`, `notifications@linear.app` or `notifications@mail.linear.app` that pass Gmail's DKIM check are linked. At most 32 links per email. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Label
attributes.text: The selected label the email was synced through. An access rule you set on the label governs its emails, including earlier thread emails fetched from All Mail. Not searchable.

example_searches: What did the customer say in their last email about the renewal?
Who was copied on the contract thread with Acme?
Which emails were about GitHub pull request 123 in our repo?

connections: A reply to the email it answers, by Message-ID.
An email to each forwarded email inside it.

A GitHub or Linear notification email to the GitHub issue or pull request, or Linear issue, it is about. GitHub items are found from the email's headers. Linear issues are found from links in the email text.
No other links to other tools.
people: Reply-To addresses and the account address are not attached as people. BCC recipients are not read.
graph.from_text: The subject, the body and the text read from attachments.

not_synced: Labels you did not select, and mailboxes Gmail marks as not selectable.
Gmail label assignments, and read and starred state.
Email older than the first sync's lookback window, unless it is an earlier email of a synced thread.
Deletions: emails deleted or moved out of a label stay in HydraDB.
A file sent as the whole email rather than as an attachment inside it.
